_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for IndiaMART InterMESH (consolidated, Rs crore). Segment model by legal entity, as the company reports it: IndiaMART standalone (the B2B marketplace, adjusted EBITDA before ESOP cost), Busy Infotech (accounting software) and Others (other subsidiaries and inter-company items, revenue only). EBITDA = segments - unallocated - ESOP, where unallocated = share of associates' losses (Screener deducts it inside expenses, so the model EBITDA equals Screener operating profit) + the EBITDA loss of the other subsidiaries. Valued on P/E, as the street does; the multiple is derived in tools/authoring/INDIAMART.ctx.js and written here by INDIAMART.val.js.

segments.name: IndiaMART (marketplace, standalone)
segments._why: Revenue = paying suppliers x ARPU, recognised from deferred revenue. FY26 +9.3% (suppliers 217K to 220K, ARPU Rs61K to Rs66K); Q1FY27 +9% with suppliers flat YoY at 218K (net -1.85K QoQ, Silver churn ~7% a month) and ARPU +8% to Rs69K. Standalone collections +10% in FY26 and +8% in Q1FY27; deferred revenue +14% YoY to Rs1,858 cr (~20% recognised within three months). Management guides 10-12% consolidated revenue growth for FY27 (May-2026) and gives no net-add guidance. We assume ARPU-led growth: +9.5% FY27E, +10% FY28-29E (flat to slightly rising suppliers, ARPU +8-9% a year from price increases and category-based Platinum pricing). MOSL models ~8-9% collection growth over FY27-28E.
segments._marginWhy: Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin (before ESOP): 40.2% FY25, 38.5% FY26, 41.5% Q1FY27 (lower acquisition spend; headcount -4% YoY). Management guides ~33% consolidated EBITDA (+/-1-2 pts) for FY27 and says sustained leverage needs subscriber growth; any return to gross adds raises sales cost. 39.5% flat gives ~33.8% consolidated (company basis) in FY27E, inside the guided band (MOSL 33.6%, Choice 33.3%).

segments.name: Busy Infotech (accounting software)
segments._why: Revenue Rs66 cr FY25, Rs119 cr FY26 (+80%: shift from perpetual licences to subscriptions; ~44% normalised), Q1FY27 Rs36 cr (+47%), deferred revenue Rs146 cr (+44%), billing +10% (Q1FY26 had ~Rs10 cr of one-off win-backs). Management: ~27-30% CAGR over the next couple of years (Q1FY27 call); ~25% (May-2026 interview). +32% FY27E (deferred revenue already booked), +27%, +25%.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 7% FY25, 17.6% FY26, 8% Q1FY27 (Busy Magic relaunch, product and team investment). 12% FY27E rising to 17% by FY29E as subscriptions scale; management expects improving margins.

segments.name: Others (subsidiaries, inter-company)
segments._why: Livekeeping and other small subsidiaries less inter-company items: revenue Rs2 cr FY25, Rs7 cr FY26, Rs3 cr Q1FY27.
segments._marginWhy: Their EBITDA (FY26 -Rs11 cr, Q1FY27 -Rs6 cr) is carried in the unallocated line.

_unallocLabel: Share of associates' losses + other subsidiaries' EBITDA loss
_unallocWhy: Associates (Vyapar, Mobisy/Bizom, Truckhall/SuperProcure, Fleetx and others, equity-accounted): Rs49 cr FY25, Rs55 cr FY26, Rs14.6 cr Q1FY27 -> Rs58 cr, Rs55 cr, Rs50 cr as the larger investees approach break-even. Others' EBITDA: +Rs5 cr FY25, -Rs11 cr FY26, -Rs6 cr Q1FY27 (Livekeeping; IndiaMART Finance being set up) -> -Rs24 cr, -Rs22 cr, -Rs20 cr. FY26 check: 555 + 21 - 35 (ESOP) - 66 = 475 = Screener operating profit.
_esopWhy: Standalone ESOP cost (adjusted less reported EBITDA): Rs17 cr FY25, Rs35 cr FY26, Rs7 cr Q1FY27 (consolidated FY26 Rs36.6 cr, AR note 21). Rs30-34 cr.
_capexWhy: Asset-light: cash capex Rs7-16 cr a year in FY23-26 and nil in Q1FY27 (company cash-utilisation slide). Rs10-12 cr.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs28.4 cr (AR note 23: PPE Rs4.8 cr, right-of-use Rs9.4 cr, Busy/Livekeeping intangibles Rs14.2 cr) = 4.3% of average gross block (Rs655 cr, which includes Rs454 cr of goodwill that is not amortised); Q1FY27 Rs6.4 cr. 4.0% gives ~Rs26-27 cr a year.

otherTreasury._why: Treasury inside Screener's other assets: inter-corporate deposits (loans Rs90 cr) and bank deposits in other financial assets (~Rs70 cr), so that Screener cash Rs91 cr + investments Rs3,792 cr + Rs160 cr = Rs4,043 cr = the company's cash and treasury investments (Rs3,280 cr) + strategic investments at book (Rs763 cr) at Mar-26 (Q1FY27 deck). Net of Rs23 cr of lease liabilities the engine's net treasury is Rs4,020 cr.

_treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to opening net treasury, which includes the Rs763 cr of strategic stakes (they earn no yield: see other income). Treasury income (debt funds, bonds, ETFs, InvITs at fair value, plus deposit interest) was Rs200 cr in FY25 (7.7% of average treasury of Rs2,613 cr) and Rs122 cr in FY26 (4.0% of Rs3,083 cr: bond mark-to-market loss of Rs34 cr net other income in Q4FY26, 'notional, would reverse'); Q1FY27 other income Rs107 cr, 'primarily mark-to-market gains on the treasury portfolio'. Through-the-cycle return on a high-grade debt book ~7%: 7.0% in FY27E (Q1 already booked), 6.75% after (repo 5.25%).
_otherIncomeWhy: Fixed items: minus the yield on the strategic stakes held inside treasury (7.0%/6.75% x Rs763 cr = -Rs53/-Rs52 cr: associates are equity-accounted and other investees are valued at fair value, not yielding) plus write-backs and interest on security deposits (~Rs3-4 cr; Rs4.4 cr FY26). Fair-value gains on strategic investments (Rs42.6 cr FY25, Rs77.7 cr FY26) and the FY25 gain on selling an associate stake (Rs29.2 cr) are one-offs and not forecast. Built FY27E other income ~Rs232 cr vs Rs204 cr reported in FY26 (Rs126 cr before strategic fair-value gains) and Rs218 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26; Q1FY27 alone Rs107 cr.
_interestWhy: Lease interest Rs2.7 cr FY26 (AR note 22, plus Rs0.3 cr on deferred consideration); Rs0.5 cr in Q1FY27. No borrowings.
_taxWhy: Effective rate on profit after associates: 26.7% FY26, 22.0% FY25 (lower-taxed capital gains), 25.8% Q1FY27. Associates' losses are not tax-deductible, so ~25% statutory becomes ~26% on our PBT.
_payoutWhy: Dividend Rs50/share for FY25 (Rs30 final + Rs20 special, 55% of EPS) and Rs60 for FY26 (Rs30 final + Rs30 special, 76%); policy: surplus capital returned by dividends or buybacks; ~40-60% of cash generated distributed over the last 3-4 years (CFO, Q4FY26 call). 60%.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, cash-rich, subscription revenue collected in advance, but a single-platform business facing churn and search/LLM disruption: 1.0 (Ke 12.5%).
dcf._tgWhy: B2B digitisation of ~1.6 crore GST-registered businesses; but the paying base is flat and AI search is a real threat to discovery: 5.5%, below nominal GDP.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 7% over 15 years (ARPU-led growth cannot compound at the current pace without customer growth).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Model EBITDA margin (after associates) ~30.5% in FY27E-29E; held at 30%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Silver churn falls and net supplier additions resume (~2-3K a quarter), category-based Platinum pricing lifts ARPU ~10% a year, and Busy keeps growing ~30% with rising margins; acquisition spend stays measured.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Buyer enquiries keep falling as search traffic moves to AI assistants, the paying-supplier base shrinks (~2K a quarter) and price rises stall; IndiaMART has to spend more on acquisition to defend the base, and Busy slows to ~15%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values IndiaMART: P/E on FY28E EPS (Choice 20x FY28E; Motilal Oswal's DCF target is ~21x its FY28E EPS). Multiple = own forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before fair-value gains on strategic investments x the sector move of the widened internet and online-classifieds set; derived in INDIAMART.ctx.js and written by INDIAMART.val.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the operating business and the treasury separately (own forward EV/EBITDA history computed in INDIAMART.ctx.js).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net treasury (incl. strategic stakes at book).

_assocShareWhy: Memo (not an engine input): the associates' share inside the unallocated line, used to show EBITDA on the company basis (model EBITDA + associates).
